title: Product Designer
description:
Product Experience Designer (Enterprise UX)
About the Role
We are seeking a Product Experience Designer to help design intuitive, scalable digital experiences for complex enterprise applications and internal business tools. This role is ideal for a designer who enjoys solving challenging workflow problems, collaborating with cross-functional teams, and creating user-centered experiences that improve productivity and efficiency.
You will partner with product managers, engineers, researchers, and stakeholders to transform business requirements into thoughtful, accessible, and impactful design solutions. From discovery through high-fidelity design and prototyping, you'll play a key role in shaping enterprise products used across large organizations.
What You'll Do

- Design end-to-end user experiences for enterprise software, internal tools, and workflow-driven applications.
- Create user flows, wireframes, prototypes, high-fidelity mockups, and design documentation in Figma.
- Support user research through interviews, usability testing, note-taking, and synthesis of findings.
- Develop journey maps, information architecture, and workflow diagrams to improve complex user experiences.
- Collaborate closely with product managers, engineers, researchers, and business stakeholders to define and prioritize solutions.
- Translate ambiguous business requirements into clear, user-centered design direction.
- Present design concepts, explain design rationale, and incorporate stakeholder and usability feedback through iterative design.
- Work within established design systems while contributing to consistency and scalability across products.
- Utilize analytics, user insights, and AI-powered design tools to continuously improve experiences and design efficiency.
- Advocate for accessibility, usability, and best practices throughout the product development lifecycle.
Qualifications

- Experience designing complex digital products, enterprise software, or internal business applications.
- Strong understanding of product experience design, enterprise UX, and systems thinking.
- Ability to quickly learn complex business domains and translate operational challenges into intuitive user experiences.
- Experience collaborating with cross-functional teams including product management, engineering, research, and business stakeholders.
- Strong communication, presentation, and storytelling skills.
- Demonstrated ability to balance user needs, technical constraints, and business objectives.
- Comfortable working in fast-paced, Agile product environments.
Required Skills

- Expert proficiency in Figma, including wireframing, visual design, prototyping, annotations, and developer handoff.
- Experience working within and contributing to design systems.
- User flow creation and journey mapping for complex, multi-step workflows.
- Strong interaction design and visual design fundamentals.
- Rapid prototyping and iterative design.

title: Senior Product Designer
description:
The YouVersion Senior Product Designer I focuses primarily on delivering well-executed design concepts and solutions to key stakeholders while creating more opportunities for people to find intimacy with God. This role uses research and intuition to help explain highly complex matters in a clear, understandable manner and ensure smooth delivery of concepts to the next stage of the design process. The Product Designer will deliver design concepts and solutions that equip teams and ministries to further Life.Church’s mission and reach people for Christ. 

 

YouVersion was created by the local church in 2007 and remains a ministry of Life.Church today. At Life.Church, our mission is to lead people to become fully devoted followers of Christ. Our team is committed to reaching people worldwide through innovative technology. And YouVersion is one of the ways we get to do that. Life.Church is a multi-site Christian church meeting in the United States and globally at Life.Church Online. 

 

We wholeheartedly believe a daily rhythm of seeking intimacy with God has the power to transform lives. That’s why YouVersion creates biblically-based experiences that encourage and challenge people to seek God. We hope everyone in our community is on an active journey to become who God made them to be, abiding in Him, and drawing closer every day. 


What You’ll Do 


- Seek and review feedback from users and empathize with their experience.

- Collaborate with project stakeholders to better understand and drive direction.

- Understand the problems we are trying to solve.

- Review, monitor, and continuously work towards achieving preset goals.

- Collaborate with product managers, product designers, and engineers to brainstorm ideas that align with our mission and goals.

- Rapidly generate multiple solutions in the form of wireframes, user flows, or prototypes that are clear and understandable.

- Create high-fidelity design comps, assets, and documentation.

- Present new design concepts to stakeholders and implement necessary feedback.

- Test prototypes with users and analyze the results.

- Produce designs that are consistent with our brand’s design system with considering the uniqueness and constraints of each platform(iOS, Android, Web, tablets, voice platforms, etc.).

- Communicate and document the myriad of states, scenarios, and edge cases of a design.

- Participate in the development process by modifying designs as needed, answering questions from engineers, testing beta software and submitting bug reports.


Skills Needed to Succeed


- Excellent verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills to foster relationships, partnerships and collaboration.

- Ability to conduct user testing and synthesize research findings for product teams.

- Ability to self-motivate, make independent decisions, and problem solve.

- Maintain flexibility and initiate the creation of new processes and project strategies.

title: UX Designer II
description:
As a Product Designer II, you'll build on foundational design skills to take ownership of small to mid-sized features across our automotive platform. You'll work closely with cross-functional teams to translate user needs into thoughtful, usable interfaces, while continuing to grow your expertise in design systems, interaction design, and user research.

You'll contribute to design critiques, collaborate on user testing, and help refine our design processes. This role is ideal for designers ready to deepen their craft and take on more responsibility in shaping product experiences.

Position Responsibilities



- Translate business requirements and user insights into intuitive, user-centered design solutions across desktop and mobile platforms.
- Assist in user research activities, including persona development, heuristic evaluations, usability reviews, and competitive analysis, to inform design decisions.
- Create and iterate on UX deliverables such as user flows, journey maps, wireframes, mockups, prototypes (low/high fidelity), and information architecture.
- Extend and apply the design system using reusable components, icon libraries, templates, and brand standards to ensure consistency and efficiency.

- Participate in agile ceremonies and workflows, providing design assets, specifications, and feedback throughout the development lifecycle.
- Support usability testing and review behavioral analytics to validate and optimize design performance.
- Maintain detailed design specifications and partner with developers to ensure accurate implementation, including involvement in user acceptance testing.
- Stay current with UX trends, tools, and technologies, and contribute to evolving team processes and design practices.
- Manage time effectively by estimating effort, planning schedules, and prioritizing tasks within sprint cycles.
- Use general-purpose LLM tools to analyze and synthesize user behavior, identify patterns, and prioritize opportunities.

Required Qualifications



- Bachelor's degree in HCI, Graphic Design, Industrial Design, or related field and 2 years' experience in a related field. The right candidate could also have a different combination, such as a master's degree and up to 2 years' experience; or 6 years' experience in a related field
- 2+ years of relevant experience designing responsive web and mobile applications, with a portfolio demonstrating thoughtful UX solutions.
- Advanced proficiency in Figma and familiarity with prototyping tools and AI-assisted design workflows.

title: Founding Product Designer
description:
Our client is a financial technology platform built for franchise and independent brand operators.

They serve a massive, underserved economy — 850,000 doors, a $4 trillion market, billions in annual spend, billions in debt originations, and billions spent every year on accounting services alone. Their platform combines expansion loans, an industry-leading charge card, and an AI-powered bookkeeping product into one integrated financial operating system.

They're an engineering and product-driven team, small and fast-moving, working on hard problems with real economic scale behind them.

Role Description

You'll design across our client's full platform — loans, cards, and the AI bookkeeper — with the bookkeeper as the center of gravity. This is a system that will sometimes be wrong, and part of the design challenge is building a front end that handles that honestly: surfacing uncertainty, inviting the user to correct us, and getting smarter because they did. You're designing the interaction that makes that correction feel seamless and inevitable, not like extra work.

Beyond the correction loop, you're designing how we communicate value — showing people, clearly and concretely, how much time and effort our product is saving them and their business.

And across the platform broadly, you're building a system and point of view for how to take genuinely complex, data-rich information and present it in a way that feels simple and intuitive.

You'll have a lot of agency here and will work closely with engineering and the leadership team, not in a silo, but as a core part of the company's overall output.

Required Qualifications



- 3–5 years of design experience, including full design ownership of a product launch, start to finish 
- Demonstrated ability to translate design decisions into behavioral outcomes: conversion, retention, activation, not just visual polish 
- Demonstrated use of AI and modern design tooling in your actual workflow, not just familiarity 
- Strong structured thinking and UX flow thinking. You can reason through a system, not just a screen 

Posted By: John Driscoll

About Flint

The best education anyone has ever received is one person paying close attention to one student: moving at their pace, noticing what they missed, asking the next question at the right moment. But the current system is built around a compromise with one teacher managing thirty students.

Flint exists to take that compromise off the table. Personalized learning, at the scale of a whole school — every student working with something closer to a tutor, and every teacher able to see what's actually happening across their class instead of guessing.

Go look at the product before you read any further: app.flintk12.com

The Role

Students want something that stays with them, going at their pace and helps them get unstuck without just handing over the answer. Teachers want that happening inside a class they still control, and they'd like their evenings back. Admins want proof that the platform they rolled out is leading to teacher productivity and student progress.

Your job is to dive deep into this design problem, holding three sets of needs within one product. We’ll trust you to ship designs that are the best possible solution to our users most urgent pain points. tl;dr you'll get to own how Flint works and how it feels.

How We Work



- We move fast, and closely. You'll work with a small, senior team: one Product Lead, a Chief of Staff (Product), a CTO, and five engineers. We also have a running joke that we can’t keep up with our #product_updates channel because of how much we ship.
- Fast and good aren't in tension here. In our experience the fastest route to something good is getting a rough version in front of a real teacher early, which tends to be quicker than getting it right in private. Decisions with the highest impact have often happened within days, not month long sprints.
- We’re always learning. Call it on-brand or a bit on the nose, but learning from each other, our customers, the market have been key to our growth. We even have channels dedicated to sharing our workflow mistakes and wins. Education is also still being actively shaped as a field, and staying tuned to what users and the industry are telling us matters more than assuming we already know.
- Users drive our decisions. Our team isn't exclusively made up of former teachers, and that's deliberate. We'd rather build from real user feedback and a range of perspectives than from any one person's classroom experience. Our close connection with teachers, students, and admins helps us quickly understand what's working and what isn't.
- We design with AI, not around it. Lo-fi concepts out of Claude, prototypes we can put in front of a teacher the same week, PRDs drafted from screenshots and voice notes: these are just a few ways we’ve used AI to support our work, and it's a real part of why our loop is as short as it is.

title: Product Designer
description:
In the 1960s, the Italian artist and inventor Bruno Munari was studying spontaneous forms: shapes that emerge from the interaction of material, function, and environment.

When Danese Milano commissioned him to design a lamp that was practical, durable, affordable, and easy to transport, Munari was reminded of the traditional rice paper lanterns he had encountered when traveling in Japan. But rice paper lanterns are fragile, hard to clean, and tend to yellow over time.

Looking for an industrial alternative, he discovered filanca—a synthetic stretch nylon used exclusively for women's stockings at the time.

Munari visited hosiery factories to test the material and see what forms it could take. "We do not make lamps, sir. Only stockings," one factory told him. Munari replied, "You'll see."

The result was the Falkland lamp: only a few centimeters thick when packaged, as tall as a human when hung, its spontaneous form emerging from the elasticity of the nylon and metal rings of different diameters inserted at regular intervals, enlarged by gravity when suspended from above.

Munari didn't begin with the form of a lamp. He began with the qualities it needed, then looked outside the conventions of lighting to find the right materials and methods. We're looking for a designer who works the same way: someone who studies the systems and materials at hand, then finds a way of putting them together that feels both unexpected and inevitable.

At Co–Star, the materials are a 4,000-year-old system of astrology, planetary data from NASA, and a corpus written by astrologers and poets. The qualities we're designing for: astrology made accessible without asking anyone to learn a complex system, and a language that lets people share something intimate with their friends.

We're hiring a Senior Product Designer to continue cultivating those qualities across Co–Star and new experiments. You'll move between product architecture, interaction design, prototyping, and visual design. Ideas rarely arrive as polished specs. You'll help decide what we make next and how it works.

What you'll do



- Design and build products from concept through launch.

What Lumion does
Lumion is the all-in-one operating system for trade and technical schools. We power the entire institution: AI-driven lead generation and conversion, enrollment, financial aid, student lifecycle management, and tuition payments. Most schools are still stitching together five or six disconnected tools to do what our platform handles.


America has a massive skilled trades shortage and the schools that train electricians, welders, and nurses are the bottleneck. We're backed by TTV Capital and Tusk Venture Partners.
Why this role matters


You would be Lumion's first dedicated product designer. Until now, design has been done by the founders, product managers, and engineers. That carried us a long way, and it is no longer enough.


Our engineers build with AI-native workflows, so the constraint on the product is no longer how fast we can write code. It is how fast we can figure out exactly what to build and make it excellent. That is design work, and right now it is our bottleneck.


The people who use our platform are admissions directors, school owners, and finance staff who live in it all day, and students making one of the bigger financial decisions of their lives. Most software in this industry was built a decade ago and looks like it. You get to set the bar for what great looks like in this market.


The work
You will own design across the entire platform.


Product design end to end. You take features from PRD to shipped: user flows, interaction design, high-fidelity UI, and specs engineers can build from without guessing. You will work directly with the CEO and CTO in design sessions and own the outcome.


Prototypes. Before engineering commits to a build, we want a working prototype in front of real schools. You will produce clickable, testable prototypes fast and use what you learn to sharpen the spec before a line of production code gets written.


The design system. The platform spans lead management, enrollment, messaging, scheduling, payments, and reporting, and it grew fast. You will build the component library and interaction patterns that make it feel like one product, and that let engineers ship good UI without a designer in the room.


AI interfaces. Schools use Lumion to configure and supervise AI agents that text, email, and call prospective students. Designing how a non-technical admissions director sets up an agent, reviews its conversations, and learns to trust it is new territory with little prior art. You will define those patterns.


Student surfaces. Enrollment applications, document signing, and tuition payments, mostly on a phone. These flows handle real money and real decisions, and they have to be effortless.

- Customer Obsession. Our customers' product is our product.

tldr: tl;dr: Fresh off a $15M Series A led by Accel (total funding now $20M+), Agave is profitable, growing fast, and scaling the team. We're hiring our first design hire to own the look, feel, and usability of Agave as we go from one product to a platform. You'll build our design system from scratch, design across every product we ship this year (2-6 new ones), and work directly with the cofounders, engineers, and PMs to make the Agave platform simple to use.

Why join us?

Early-stage, yet de-risked. We are a rare combo of being early stage (high upside) but lower risk (5XX+ paying customers, $Xm+ recurring revenue, profitable & cash-flow positive for over 2 years, hockey-stick growth). You get the benefits of an early stage startup without the risk you'll have at almost any other startup. You'll have a ton of impact, work directly with our customers, and ship real product for real users. Although we're early stage, we've eliminated the key strategic risks you'll face at other startups — unproven product, lack of market validation, lack of revenue, over-reliance on VC funding, co-founder disputes. We're all young and hungry. Our team is fully in-person, tenacious, and committed — most of us moved to SF from far away (Canada, SoCal, Texas, Virginia) specifically to build Agave from the ground up.

A blank canvas with real stakes. Most first design hires join companies that are either pre-product (nothing to design for) or post-product (constrained by whatever was built before you). We're in the sweet spot. We have 2 live products customers already love, and 2-6 more launching this year. You'll build all of our design system, component library, and product surface it, and every product shipping for the next several years will carry your fingerprints.

Your work compounds. Every product you design plugs into infrastructure we've spent years building, and every new product makes the rest of our suite more valuable. You're not designing in a vacuum — you're designing for an existing customer base, a co-sell network with some of the largest companies in construction, and a platform that's still being defined. The decisions you make in your first six months will shape how thousands of construction teams interact with their critical software for years.

Huge opportunity with little direct competition. Startups are incredibly hard, so you want to join one that has a unique advantage. Construction is the world's third-largest industry and overlooked by most people in startup land. We have a multi-year head start against potential competitors. We're backed by world-class investors (Accel, YC) and construction insiders (Procore and Autodesk executives, founders of the largest construction tech companies like PlanGrid).

Our work initially focused on the entertainment industry, specifically live events and recorded music (SXSW, Sony Music, Universal Music, and Disney Music Group are all clients). We have grown to include global brands (Amazon, Sophia Learning), major sports franchises (X Games, Florida Panthers, Washington Commanders, Cleveland Cavaliers, Women’s Tennis Association), as well as public sector institutions (City of Boston, Massachusetts Office of Travel and Tourism).


Gupta Media is seeking a Designer who is excited to connect with audiences across multiple visual mediums —digital ad campaigns, OOH, web, events, motion/video, print, social, and other ways we haven’t yet thought of. - Ability to carry projects from concept to completion, working collaboratively across teams on ideation, creation, and implementation;

- A strong communicator, able to present your ideas to internal and external teams;

To apply, please submit a resume, portfolio of relevant work, and a quick note on why you are the perfect candidate for Gupta Media.


Work Environment
Gupta Media is an office-first organization.


Our Commitment
At Gupta Media, we work hard every day to be better at all that we do — and that includes fostering a diverse and inclusive community that encourages and respects a broad range of backgrounds, experiences, and ideas.


Compensation
At Gupta Media, base salary is one component of our total compensation and benefits package. For this role, the anticipated base salary range is $58,000 - $70,000, depending on relevant experience, skills, and qualifications. This role is eligible to participate in our annual bonus plan, which is based on the company's performance.

title: Product Designer, Enterprise
description:
About Us

Our mission is to reinvent the way people learn, starting with language.

Learning a language can change a life by opening doors to new cultures, careers, and communities. Two billion people around the world are actively trying to learn a language, but the best way to learn (one-on-one tutoring) is hard to access at scale and hasn’t been meaningfully improved in decades. Speak is building a human-level, AI-powered tutor in your pocket: a conversation-first experience that lets learners actually speak, get instant feedback, and progress through carefully designed lessons. The result is a complete path from beginner to confident speaker across multiple languages.

Speak first launched in South Korea in 2019, where Speak has now become the number one language learning app, and we now serve learners across many markets and 15+ languages. Speak is one of the world’s leading AI companies, with over $150m raised in venture investment from OpenAI, Accel, Founders Fund, Khosla Ventures, and more, with a distributed team across San Francisco, Seoul, Tokyo, Taipei, and Ljubljana.

About The Design Team

We’re a small, high-craft team of six working at the intersection of research, invention, and product thinking. We build consumer and B2B experiences used by millions across 150+ markets — and a lot of the work is genuinely novel: inventing how someone talks to an AI tutor, what feedback feels like when you’re learning out loud, and how progress should be measured and celebrated.

We stay close to learners through prototyping, interviews, betas, and experiments. We take craft seriously, iterate fast, and value a high-trust critique-and-build culture. We have something to prove — and design awards to win.

Role & responsibilities

Speak’s enterprise product is still early, but the problem is big: companies need to know whether their teams are actually building language proficiency, where learners are getting stuck, and what interventions will help. You’ll help define the tools they use to launch programs, understand progress, spot risks, and prove that language learning is working.



- Shape the strategy and design of our company-facing product — the admin, reporting, and account experiences the L&D managers who buy Speak rely on to launch, run, and prove their programs

title: Staff Product Designer
description:
Overview

About the Team

The Tech Business Disruption team explores bold new frontiers in technology and business models to uncover growth opportunities that shape Intuit's future. We incubate breakthrough product concepts, experiment with emerging technologies, and identify disruptive trends that redefine how we deliver value to our customers and accelerate innovation across the company. Our work is fast-moving, ambiguous by design, and high-leverage. We move from insight to working prototype quickly, and the things we ship today will help inform Intuit's portfolio years from now.

About The Role

We're looking for a Staff Product Designer who's passionate about translating transformative insights into innovative product experiences. You'll apply qualitative and quantitative understanding to identify unmet user needs, emerging interaction patterns, and market shifts, helping teams design, prototype, and validate disruptive concepts that challenge the status quo.

This role calls for a curious, strategic designer who thrives in ambiguity, connects design patterns across industries, and inspires cross-functional teams to turn insights into impactful designs. You should be ready to roll up your sleeves to ship a working prototype by the end of week.

Responsibilities



- Lead initiatives of significant scope and complexity working with the lead designer on the creative vision, strategy, and execution from earliest concept through validated prototype.
- Synthesize behavioral data, customer research, and industry signals to imagine experiences as they might be, not as they are.
- Apply strategic thinking to deliver innovative end-to-end user experiences that balance user needs, business goals, and technological realities across web and mobile.
- Translate ambiguous concepts into wireframes, interaction models, high-fidelity designs, and prototypes that communicate compellingly to internal leaders, partners, and customers.
- Partner closely with product managers, engineers, and researchers to move from hypothesis to learning as quickly as possible.
- Use rapid prototyping, including AI-assisted tools and lightweight code, to test feasibility, generate excitement, and de-risk new directions.
- Solicit and contribute thoughtful, candid feedback in design reviews, and use facilitative leadership to drive teams toward the best outcome for customers.
- Advance a clear point of view backed by personal expertise, design rationale, customer data, and industry trends.
- Manage multiple concurrent explorations, balancing depth of craft with speed of learning.

Qualifications

Qualifications



- 8+ years of experience in product design, with a portfolio that demonstrates strong end-to-end craft across interaction, visual, and prototyping work.
- Bachelor's degree in Design, HCI, Human Factors, Design Strategy, or equivalent practical experience.
- Demonstrated expertise applying user-centered design processes while collaborating with customers and cross-funct

title: Senior Product Designer, Consumer
description:
Discord has a highly engaged community of millions of daily active users who use the platform for many different reasons, but there’s one thing that nearly everyone does: play video games. Discord plays a uniquely important role in the future of gaming, and we are focused on making it easier and more fun for people to hang out before, during, and after playing games.

Our mission on the Consumer team is to improve both the quality and depth of Discord’s core product value - which is to make Discord the best place to hang out online and play games with friends. Millions of people use Discord every day to find belonging, create connections, and talk… and we are the center of this.

The work focuses on improving and simplifying the foundations of the Discord experience at large. This could be streamlining how users customize their settings, to the way they express themselves over text, voice, and video. You’ll be part of a multi-faceted team flexing across surface area ownership, and acting as a guardian on our core foundations.

As a product designer, you'll be involved with the full end-to-end product development process, from brainstorming to launch. You'll use a balance of strategic thinking, product principles, systems design, and strong visual design skills to iterate and innovate on the Discord product. If you're interested in joining a passionate team of designers that are designing features that will be used by millions of people across the world, come join us.

This position will be located in the San Francisco Bay Area (Alameda, Contra Costa, Marin, Napa, San Francisco, San Mateo, Santa Clara, Solano, and Sonoma Counties), or be willing to relocate to the San Francisco Bay Area.

What You'll Be Doing

description:
LA28 does not provide relocation assistance.

LA28 is the independent, non-profit, privately funded organizing committee for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic and Paralympic Games. We are on a singular mission to create an Olympic and Paralympic Games that celebrate all that this city and country have to offer, delivering an unparalleled experience for athletes, fans, partners and our community.

The 2028 Games mark the return of the Summer Games to the U.S. for the first time in 32 years and Los Angeles’ third time hosting an Olympic Games and first time welcoming the Paralympic Games. This presents the unique and exciting opportunity to celebrate our legacy with the Games and push the Olympic and Paralympic Movements forward, writing a new chapter of Games history in Los Angeles.

Putting on an Olympic and Paralympic Games is a team sport. To build a Games unlike any the world has seen before, we need the best team in place–a team full of perspectives, experiences and expertise. We are guided by the following set of values and behaviors–optimism, integrity, excellence, inclusion, co-creation and boldness–and look forward to hearing about how your past experiences align with them.

The Brand, Identity and Look of the Games (BIL) team is responsible for overseeing the development and management of all LA28' visual identity. Our work defines how the Games are seen and remembered—through a variable emblem system, typography, color palette, imagery, patterns, and more—creating a brand experience that is bold, distinctive, and timeless.

The LA28 brand is the first-ever variable Olympic and Paralympic logo and has an ever-expanding inventory of design assets. Along with developing and managing the core identity, the BIL team is responsible for marquee Games design deliverables such as core graphic, pictograms, and torch in addition to internal creative services.

We are executing a complex Figma design system migration—moving a large, interconnected Figma environment from one enterprise account to another. The work involves shared libraries, component hierarchies, and a token architecture managed through Token Studio. 
We are seeking a Figma specialist with deep design systems expertise to lead this effort. You will be embedded with our design team, working hands-on through every phase of the migration. - Execute Figma’s Swap Library feature across the full file set to reconnect components after the Foundations library is migrated to the new account
- Identify and manually resolve components that cannot be automatically matched during the swap (including renamed, deleted, or structurally changed assets)
- Validate the published state of all Patterns, Recipes, and Template libraries post-migration to ensure downstream files receive updates correctly
- Document all library decisions, known gaps, and structural changes for the broader design team
 Token & Variable Work

- Ensure the token architecture supports a scalable, independent design system
 Migration Execution

- Coordinate with organizational admins for team-level transfers to the new enterprise account

- Perform full QA on the migrated environment prior to handoff, ensuring no broken references, missing libraries, or disconnected tokens

title: Senior Product Designer

About Nuvo

Nuvo is building the infrastructure that powers trade in the physical goods economy.

Every part of modern life depends on physical goods: the food we eat, the fabric we wear, the steel and concrete that shape our cities. Behind it all are 50 million businesses trading $100 trillion each year.

Consider how housing gets built. One company cuts down trees, another turns the wood into building materials, another sells the product wholesale, and a contractor uses them to build homes. Each step is a business trading with another to turn raw materials into finished goods.

Most of these businesses still operate through offline networks, held together by fragmented systems, manual processes, and institutional memory. When trade is slow, costly, or error-prone, the effects cascade — resources get misallocated, businesses can’t grow, and consumers face higher costs and fewer choices.

Nuvo builds technology that makes trade fast, automated, and intelligent. More than 75,000 businesses already use our platform, and we’re backed by $45M from Sequoia, Spark, Founders Fund, and Index as we build the operating system for global commerce.

As a Senior Product Designer, you’ll shape how this system comes to life for thousands of businesses, defining how complex operations become simple, intuitive, and powerful.

You’ll operate with deep ownership, collaborating closely with engineering, product, and customer teams. You’ll help define the next generation of experiences that make Nuvo increasingly compelling across new industries and use cases.

title: Visual Design Apprentice

Visual Design Apprentice


The Short Version
You make things beautiful. Not “clean and modern” beautiful. Stop-scrolling, zoom-in, who-made-this beautiful. You'll design the visual identity systems, product interfaces, and brand assets for ventures that don't exist yet.


What Liminal Is
A Founders' Studio. We co-build with repeat founders, many of them unicorn founders, providing build expertise, capital, and unfair access from founding to Series B. We call ourselves a Founders' Studio because “venture studio” undersells what we do and oversells what most of them deliver.


What This Role Actually Is
Dirty secret in design hiring: the Venn of great visual and great UX designers barely overlaps. We hire for the visual circle. Emphatically.


You build the visual layer for a venture: identity, interfaces, decks, assets. You turn positioning into something a founder looks at and says "that's us." You sweat what others don't see. Optical alignment. The weight of whitespace. Why one shade of blue reads "trustworthy fintech" and the one three hex values over reads "dental office."


The Work

- Visual identity and brand systems. Translate brand strategy into complete visual identities: typography, color, layout grids, iconography, the overall look and feel that makes a venture cohesive across every touchpoint.
- Product and digital surfaces. Design clean, visually engaging UI for early-stage products: landing pages, dashboards, onboarding flows, marketing pages. You own the high-fidelity output and work directly with engineering so what ships looks like what you designed.
- Brand assets at scale. Decks, social content, one-pagers, investor materials, event collateral. Often the first thing the outside world sees. They need to be flawless.
- Design system stewardship. Build and maintain coherent design languages that hold up as the venture grows, so the hundredth asset looks as considered as the first.


Who You Are

- Exceptional visual craft. A portfolio that makes us lean in. Strong command of typography, color theory, composition, and layout across brand and digital surfaces. You know the difference between beautiful and merely pretty. You can explain why, in terms that aren't just vibes.
- Exquisite taste. Omnivorous and opinionated. You have feelings about restaurant menus, movie title sequences, transit signage, and the packaging on your toothpaste. Your taste is informed by what you've consumed across design, art, architecture, fashion, and culture. Not just what Dribbble served you last week.
- Tool fluency. Figma and Adobe Creative Suite are second nature. You work fast, iterate without preciousness, and produce high-fidelity output that doesn't need a translator between you and engineering.
- Comfort with ambiguity. No brand guides. No existing design systems. No “make it like the last one.” A founder, a blank page, and a company that needs to look like it was inevitable. That should thrill you.
- Contrarian streak. Independent thinker. Arg

Every civilization runs on the same infrastructure: agreements between people who don't fully trust each other. Sumerians pressed them into clay. Romans carved them into stone. We bury them in 80-page PDFs.

Familiarity with the Adobe Creative Suite.

title: Founding Product Designer

-  Full-Time

About Andromeda

Andromeda Cluster was founded by Nat Friedman and Daniel Gross to give early-stage startups access to the kind of scaled AI infrastructure once reserved only for hyperscalers.

We began with a single managed cluster — but it filled almost instantly. Since then, we've been quietly building the systems, network, and orchestration layer that makes the world's AI infrastructure more accessible.

Today, Andromeda works with leading AI labs, data centers, and cloud providers to deliver compute when and where it's needed most. Our platform routes training and inference jobs across global supply, unlocking flexibility and efficiency in one of the fastest-growing markets on earth.

Our long-term vision is to build the liquidity layer for global AI compute. We are expanding to new frontiers to find the brightest that work in AI infrastructure, research and engineering.

The Role

You will be our first full-time designer. A part-time designer drove our original designs; you'll build on that work and own design from here: a developer-facing compute platform, the console where teams find, buy, and run GPU capacity across global supply. The work is dense and technical, closer to GitHub, GitLab, or Vercel than to a consumer app.

This is a hands-on IC role. You'll report to the Head of Product and work closely with the leadership team. There is no design team to manage yet; as we grow, you'll have the opportunity to build one. Your first job is to establish design as a core function of the company. The design system and product language you create will shape Andromeda for years.

- End-to-end product design: Take problems from research to shipped UI. You'll pair with engineers through implementation and review what ships. 
- The design system: Take over our existing system and mature it. Tokens, components, and patterns for dense, data-rich surfaces: capacity and pricing tables, usage and billing views, cluster and job dashboards. 
- The developer experience: Every surface a customer touches. Console, dashboards, onboarding, docs, terminal, and the places where the product meets the terminal. Cut the time from signup to first running workload. 
- Design direction: Set the visual language, interaction patterns, and quality bar for the whole product. Run critique. Later, help hire the team.

- 5+ years designing software, with recent work on developer tools, infrastructure, or technical B2B products. 
- A portfolio of dense, data-rich UIs for expert users: consoles, dashboards, tables, logs. Information density over whitespace. 
- Design systems experience: You've built one, or shipped major contributions to one. Not just consumed one. 
- You ship in ambiguity: You go from a rough idea to a high-fidelity product on your own, and you'd rather ship this week than polish next quarter.

- You want to manage first: This is an IC rol

title: Product Manager, Connect
description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About The Product - Connect Platform

Connect is Stripe’s platform for businesses that serve other businesses. It gives platforms the infrastructure to represent the people and companies in their ecosystem, onboard and verify them, manage their accounts, accept payments, and pay them out - without building payments, compliance, or financial-services systems themselves. This is how businesses like Shopify can help entrepreneurs run and grow their businesses. It is also the kind of infrastructure that marketplaces such as DoorDash need to coordinate money movement across large networks of restaurants, merchants, and dashers.

Connect has impact across industries. Shopify uses Stripe to embed financial services for merchants; Lugg streamlines worker onboarding and offers instant payouts; DoorLoop reduces manual customer onboarding tasks by nearly 50% with Stripe; and Sharetribe helps entrepreneurs launch and run marketplaces on Stripe.

AI is accelerating the emergence of entirely new business models: global networks of creators and experts, AI-native marketplaces, and agent-driven products that change how people discover, buy, sell, and deliver services. These businesses are more dynamic than traditional platforms: participants may operate across borders, take on different roles, and need new ways to establish trust, access financial capabilities, and get paid.

The Connect Abstractions team owns the platform primitives that make these models possible. We are building the foundational abstractions for representing participants, onboarding them safely, configuring their capabilities, and managing their lifecycle on Stripe. Our work will determine how quickly the next generation of platforms can launch, how flexibly they can evolve, and how much of Stripe they can bring to the businesses and people they serve.

Why this role

This is a chance to define a foundational product area at Stripe. You will turn a fast-changing set of user and product needs into durable platform primitives that work across products, industries, and geographies.

The role combines high-leverage strategy with hands-on product execution. You will work through ambiguous, consequential questions like: what should a platform be able to model? What should be simple by default but flexible when needed? How can Stripe make complex financial infrastructure feel effortless for a platform and its users?

description:
Apparel Graphic Designer – Basketball & Sportswear

We are seeking a talented Apparel Graphic Designer to join a global sportswear design team focused on creating innovative, consumer-driven graphics for basketball-inspired apparel collections. This designer will play a key role in developing original artwork, visual stories, and graphic concepts that connect with athletes, fans, and sport culture worldwide.

The ideal candidate is a creative storyteller with a strong background in apparel graphic design, particularly tee-shirt and print-focused graphics. They should have a passion for basketball, a strong understanding of cultural and visual trends, and a portfolio demonstrating original design work across typography, illustration, layouts, and branded graphics.

What You’ll Do



- Create original apparel graphics for basketball-focused collections, including typography, illustrations, logos, marks, and seasonal graphic concepts 
- Develop compelling visual narratives that connect with athletes, consumers, and sport culture 
- Lead the creative process from concept development through final execution 
- Build graphic design presentations, visual concepts, and seasonal design stories 
- Collaborate with cross-functional partners including product, development, and design teams 
- Research cultural, sport, and graphic design trends to inspire new creative directions 
- Participate in brainstorms, design reviews, and product creation meetings 

What You’ll Bring



- 5+ years of experience in apparel graphic design, with a strong focus on tee-shirt graphics and print-based design 
- A portfolio showcasing original apparel graphics, typography, illustrations, layouts, and visual storytelling 
- Strong proficiency in Adobe Photoshop and Illustrator 
- Deep understanding of graphic design principles including typography, color, composition, and brand identity 
- Passion for basketball, sports culture, and consumer trends 
- Ability to translate creative concepts and stories into impactful product graphics 
- Strong collaboration and communication skills with the ability to present and articulate design ideas 

Nice To Have



- Experience designing for sportswear, streetwear, or lifestyle brands 
- Experience with AI visualization tools and emerging creative technologies 
- Familiarity with 3D design tools such as CLO or similar platforms 
- Experience supporting athlete collections, collaborations, or seasonal product launches 

This is an opportunity for a highly creative designer to influence the future of basketball apparel graphics and create work that resonates with athletes and fans around the world.

Client Description

Global leader in athletic footwear, apparel, and equipment. Our client focuses on innovation, performance, and marketing, partnering with top athletes and teams. The company emphasizes sustainability and digital advancements to enhance the sports experience.

About The Role

Artemis Security is hiring a Product Designer to shape how security teams actually use our platform. In cybersecurity, most tools are built by engineers for engineers, and it shows - dense UIs, buried workflows, and dashboards no one actually looks at. We're building something different: a platform that security teams reach for because it's genuinely well-designed, not just powerful.

You'll own the end-to-end product experience across the Artemis platform, from the earliest concept sketches through pixel-perfect execution. You'll partner directly with our founders, product, and engineering leadership on the decisions that shape how the product feels, flows, and gets used every day. This is a role for a designer who thrives in complexity: security work generates enormous volumes of information, and you'll need a strong command of visual hierarchy — knowing what to foreground, what to tuck away, and how to make dense, data-rich interfaces feel clear and navigable.

Just as important is connective thinking: designing intuitive links between different areas of the product so teams can move fluidly from signal to investigation to response without losing context. You'll design for a technical, high-stakes audience — CISOs, security architects, SOC analysts — where clarity and trust matter more than flourish.

- Own product design end to end for the Artemis platform, from research and discovery through interaction design, visual polish, and hand-off

- Build and evolve our design system so product velocity increases as we grow, without sacrificing quality or consistency
- Lead user research with security practitioners, from customer calls and shadowing sessions to structured usability testing
- Contribute to product strategy by bringing a strong point of view on what to build, not just how to build it
- Work closely with our brand and marketing designers to ensure the product experience feels like a natural extension of the Artemis brand

- 5+ years of product design experience at an enterprise SaaS company, with meaningful ownership of complex, workflow-heavy products
- A portfolio that demonstrates strong end-to-end product thinking, not just visual polish — clear examples of research, tradeoffs, and shipped work
- Experience designing for technical or expert users (developers, security teams, data teams, IT admins, or similar), where dense information and complex workflows are the norm

title: Senior Product Designer
description:
About PactFi

Private asset markets (PE, Private Credit, VC, Real Estate) have 10x to 9.8T in AUM over the past decade and are projected to grow to $17T in the next five years. However, digital infrastructure has not kept pace, with most of the market operating predominantly in error-prone, internal-only software solutions.

PactFi provides secure, end-to-end, operational infrastructure for managing complex private credit transactions. Our web-based application brings together all parties involved in such a transaction to more efficiently allocate capital, complete KYC, share documents, manage funds flow, and more. The platform is secured to a bank-grade standard, and we have received our SOC 2 Type 2 attestation.

PactFi was developed in close partnership with two of the industry's largest players, both of whom represent the top 3 players in the private credit space by both size (AUM) and deal activity.

The Design Problem



- Product is moving from a screen-first build model, where the underlying system is designed first and the interface follows. 
- Today's product is fully deterministic, human-driven screens. You'd help define, from scratch, what this platform looks like as AI becomes a first-class part of it — AI agents as a new type of participant alongside human users, and AI as a new interaction modality for human users themselves. 
- Workflows are tied to assets that can live 5–7 years, resurfacing repeatedly at different cadences over that lifetime, with multiple parties holding different views and permissions each time. 
- Clients regularly bring new deal and asset structures the platform hasn't seen before, so the product has to accommodate structural variation it can't fully anticipate. 
- Permissioning is layered — participants often have their own downstream stakeholders who need visibility into a subset of the same information. 
- A point of view on how AI is reshaping what a "product" is — where a great interface is still needed versus where the underlying data itself, exposed well, is becoming the product — is a plus. 

What You'll Do



- Own one or two major product surfaces end-to-end — from problem framing through shipped, polished detail. 
- Design and ship the platform's first real AI-native interaction pattern in an otherwise fully deterministic product — no existing pattern to extend from. 
- Design for dense, structured financial data at scale, and for multi-party, long-running workflows with layered permissions. 
- Work closely with the PM and engineers on your surface to develop the strategy and rationale behind what you build, not just execute a spec. 
- Contribute to and help shape a design system built for extensibility across evolving workflows and asset structures. 
- Set an example in critique and day-to-day work for how design is done here — the work itself is the signal, not a title or mandate.

- World-class team: We seek high agency contributors who are comfortable navigating ambiguity, ruthlessly prioritize what matters and are action-biased.
- Grow with us: We reward impact, not credentials or years of experience. We intend to grow talent from within as we scale up.
- Competitive pay and benefits: top compensation with full benefits including:

title: Senior Product Designer
description:
In the 1960s, the Italian artist and inventor Bruno Munari was studying spontaneous forms: shapes that emerge from the interaction of material, function, and environment.

When Danese Milano commissioned him to design a lamp that was practical, durable, affordable, and easy to transport, Munari was reminded of the traditional rice paper lanterns he had encountered when traveling in Japan. But rice paper lanterns are fragile, hard to clean, and tend to yellow over time.

Looking for an industrial alternative, he discovered filanca—a synthetic stretch nylon used exclusively for women's stockings at the time.

Munari visited hosiery factories to test the material and see what forms it could take. "We do not make lamps, sir. Only stockings," one factory told him. Munari replied, "You'll see."

The result was the Falkland lamp: only a few centimeters thick when packaged, as tall as a human when hung, its spontaneous form emerging from the elasticity of the nylon and metal rings of different diameters inserted at regular intervals, enlarged by gravity when suspended from above.

Munari didn't begin with the form of a lamp. He began with the qualities it needed, then looked outside the conventions of lighting to find the right materials and methods. We're looking for a designer who works the same way: someone who studies the systems and materials at hand, then finds a way of putting them together that feels both unexpected and inevitable.

At Co–Star, the materials are a 4,000-year-old system of astrology, planetary data from NASA, and a corpus written by astrologers and poets. The qualities we're designing for: astrology made accessible without asking anyone to learn a complex system, and a language that lets people share something intimate with their friends.

We're hiring a Senior Product Designer to continue cultivating those qualities across Co–Star and new experiments. You'll move between product architecture, interaction design, prototyping, and visual design. Ideas rarely arrive as polished specs. You'll help decide what we make next and how it works.

What you'll do:



- Own major product surfaces end-to-end: concept, flows, interaction, visual polish, ship
- Invent interaction paradigms for things that haven't existed before and moke those new paradigms legible and fun

- Prototype constantly, in Figma and in code — we expect tools like Claude Code, Cursor, and v0 to be part of your workflow 
- Partner directly with engineering and research, to refine interactions, iterate quickly, and ship high-quality work.

You might be a fit if:



- You've spent the last decade designing software people love to use.
- You're comfortable moving between interaction design, visual design, and product thinking.

145,000 - 175,000 USD per year(Moon HQ)

The Junior Graphic Designer should possess a solid understanding of printed materials, production techniques, and file preparation. These materials include packaging, labeling, large-format prints, stickers, and more. While the role has a primary focus on print design, it also supports projects via digital deliverables within a 360-degree media landscape.

This position will be based in Philadelphia, PA and going into the office on a hybrid schedule.

- Execute & Innovate: Drive creative innovation and execute print techniques aligned with the UO aesthetic lens.
- Production & Prep: Focus heavily on file preparation, mock-ups, tech packs, informational details, and creating compelling presentations for assignments.
- Market Research: Research competitors and gather inspiration, clearly communicating design intent while offering diverse production solutions.
- Trend Analysis: Stay mindful of current design trends and concepts, actively seeking opportunities to help expand the UO design point of view.
- Brand Stewardship: Help maintain brand standards, organization, and visual cohesion across all assets.
- Project Management: Communicate project statuses clearly and manage shifting priorities effectively.
- File Maintenance: Preflight, collect, upload, and download project assets while organizing files in a clean, highly usable manner.

Role Qualifications



- Experience: 1–2 years of professional graphic design experience.
- Technical Skills: Working knowledge of Adobe Creative Cloud (Illustrator, Photoshop, InDesign), Figma, and Google Workspace.
- Production Knowledge: Strong understanding of print, prepress production, and file preparation.
- Design Eye: A keen eye for typography, layout, and visual hierarchy.
- Soft Skills: Excellent communication skills, a highly collaborative mindset, and strong professional etiquette.
- Problem Solving: Proven ability to problem-solve, adapt quickly, and effectively follow art direction.
- Time Management: Highly organized with the ability to manage multiple projects and timelines simultaneously across shifting seasonal deadlines.

title: Freelance Presentation Designer
description:
Please submit your resume in English and indicate your level of English.

Mindrift is looking for a highly skilled Presentation Designer to join the Tendem project (**https://tendem.ai/**) and drive specialized storytelling workflows within our hybrid AI + human system.

In this role, you'll collaborate with Tendem Agents that handle repetitive tasks, while you provide the critical thinking, domain expertise, and formatting skills necessary to deliver beautifully designed, high-stakes presentations.

This part-time remote opportunity is ideal for creative professionals with hands-on experience in visual communications, information design, and storytelling.

What We Do

The Mindrift platform connects specialists with AI projects from major tech innovators. Our mission is to unlock the potential of Generative AI by tapping into real-world expertise from across the globe.

About The Role

This is a freelance role for a Tendem project. As a Presentation Designer, you will focus on storytelling and visual hierarchy. We need a specialist who knows how to communicate complex information beautifully, turning raw data and narratives into compelling, highly persuasive slides and one-pagers. You will utilize various tools such as PowerPoint, Keynote, alongside Adobe Creative Suite or Figma.

Key Responsibilities



- Design high-stakes pitch decks and professional one-pagers tailored for specific audiences. 
- Translate complex data into clear visual storytelling with a strong focus on minimalism and precise information hierarchy. 
- Elevate presentations using custom fonts, elegant animations, and perfect visual consistency. 
- Enforce a polished, persuasive, and premium corporate-meets-creative style across all deliverables. 
- Execute formatting quality standards through meticulous validation of visual alignment, pacing, and brand adherence before final delivery. 

How To Get Started

Apply, pass qualification(s), and start contributing to projects aligned with your expertise — on your own schedule.

Requirements



- At least 2 years of relevant experience in graphic design, presentation design, visual storytelling, or data visualization is desirable
- Bachelor's or Master's Degree in Graphic Design, Fine Arts, Visual Communications, or related creative fields is a plus
- Presentation software: Expertise in PowerPoint, Keynote, etc., for building complex, dynamic, and perfectly animated decks. 
- Design tools: Deep proficiency with Adobe Creative Suite (Illustrator, Photoshop) or Figma to create custom graphics and layouts. 
- Data & information design: Ability to translate complex data and multi-level hierarchical structures into clear, minimalist visual storytelling. 
- Typography & animation: Advanced skills in working with custom fonts and smooth, elegant animations for premium deliverables
- English proficiency: Upper-intermediate (B2) or above (required)

Additional Requirements



- Hands-on experience creating high-end, premium corporate

title: Junior Production Designer
description:
Fresh Tape Media is looking for a Junior Production Designer to join our Denver-based team. Fresh Tape Media works with brands, sports properties, and media companies to produce one-of-a-kind, made-for-social content. From quick-turn productions to fully custom builds, we help brands drive engagement by creating content people actually want to watch and share and memorialize a moment!


This role is ideal for someone early in their career who has foundational production design skills, some hands-on experience, and is ready to take on more responsibility with some of the most iconic brand names in the world! You’ll support the production team across a variety of projects, contributing to concept development, set design, on-set execution and liaising with vendors & fabrication partners. An eye for design (interior, spatial, experiential, or production) and a proactive, team-first attitude are essential.


Responsibilities include:
Research & Concept Development

- Support the development of visual references, mood boards, and design directions for projects
- Contribute ideas during early concepting phases
- Assist in testing materials and approaches for feasibility and execution


Set Design & Planning

- Create sketches, mocks, technical drawings and 3D models (Adobe Suite, SketchUp, LayOut, V-Ray preferred)
- Help build and refine production design presentations for internal and client-facing use
- Maintain organized production design documentation across projects
- Be able to answer internal and external questions to production design approach confidently


Prop & Material Sourcing

- Source props, set decor, and materials aligned with creative direction and budget
- Communicate with vendors, rental houses, and fabricators for quotes, availability, and identify any opportunities for efficiencies
- Track purchased and rented items, helping maintain inventory across projects
- Coordinate logistics for deliveries, pickups, and returns
- Develop and maintain a knowledge base of vendors, their product ranges and policies pertaining to shipping, delivery and returns


On-Set Execution

- Assist in building, assembling, and styling sets on shoot days
- Support prop placement and ensure visual consistency with the intended design
- Help troubleshoot design challenges in real-time during production
- Participate in strike and breakdown, including planning for reuse or storage of materials
- Support Production Designer on larger, more complex activations
- Assist the Production Designer in coordinating Art Department members and logistics as needed
- Occasionally represent Fresh Tape Media as the sole on-site Production Designer for activations


Basic Qualifications:

- Strong portfolio with spec work and/or realized concepts
- 2 years of relevant experience (internships, freelance, academic work, or entry-level roles count!)
- Basic knowledge of on-set etiquette and protocols is desirable
- Working knowledge of Photoshop, G-suite, Sketc

Skilled across a range of design styles—from classic to contemporary—Designers utilize digital tools and technology during in-store and in-home consultations to bring customer visions to life. We're living through a fundamental shift in how people discover, evaluate, and purchase products. The next generation doesn't respond to traditional marketing -- they build relationships with brands through authentic social interactions, seek recommendations from communities they trust, and expect personalized experiences that feel human, not corporate.

At Nectar Social, we're building the AI-native social operating system that enables this new era of commerce. We believe every social interaction should deepen the relationship between brands and their communities while creating genuine value for both sides.

Founded by ex-Meta product and engineering leaders, we've raised over $30M in total capital from investors including GV and True Ventures. We work with brands like Oura Health, Caraway, e.l.f. Cosmetics, Kosas, OLIPOP, and many more. We're building the future of social commerce -- where community, conversation, and commerce converge.

The Role

As Nectar's first Brand Designer, you won't be joining an existing design system; you'll be defining it. This is a rare chance to build the visual foundation of a category-defining AI company at the exact moment it's stepping into a much bigger spotlight.

You'll work directly with the co-founders as the design point of contact for brand and marketing, with your fingerprints on everything from the identity system to the product's early visual language. The scope is intentionally broad: this is a builder's role, not a maintainer's.

What You'll Do



- Define and evolve Nectar's visual identity (logo, typography, color, iconography, motion) into a system flexible enough to work across web, product, social, and print
- Own brand execution across the website, landing pages, pitch decks, one-pagers, and sales collateral
- Design social and campaign creative that captures Nectar's voice across launches, announcements, and always-on content

- Partner closely with founders, marketing, and early product/engineering hires to keep brand and product experience consistent

- 4+ years of brand or visual design experience, ideally including startup or agency work spanning multiple brand touchpoints
- A portfolio that demonstrates systems thinking, featuring cohesive identities that hold together across many formats, not just standalone pieces
- Comfort setting direction with little existing process: you'll be writing the playbook, not just following one
- Strong typography, layout, and color instincts; fluency in Figma (motion/video tools a plus)

description:
We're Heidi.

We're building the future of healthcare by giving every clinician the earth's finest AI Care Partner. In just 18 months, our clinical AI products have absorbed the administrative chaos of 73 million patient visits. Today, we support over 2.5 million patient sessions a week across 190+ countries.

Healthcare systems are failing us; clinicians spend more time on documentation than on patients, and the human connection that makes medicine worth practicing is eroding.

Our mission is simple: double the world's healthcare capacity and strengthen the human connection at its heart.

We found product-market fit with a freemium medical scribe that clinicians love. Now, we're expanding. Every task a clinician hands to Heidi is a patient who feels more attended to, a health system unclogged, and a clinician who gets to be a clinician again.

If you don't choose easy and you want to build something way bigger than yourself then, choose the challenge, choose Heidi.

The role

We're looking for a product designer who designs, prototypes, and ships — and knows the difference between software that works and software that makes someone smile.

Clinicians use Heidi to get away from keyboards and back to patients. We want the product to feel as considered as the best software you've ever used — cohesive, quiet, and precise across every surface. When a clinician's tools feel right, they spend less time fighting software and more time with patients. That's the job.

This role sits close to the front line. You'll be designing directly against real customer requests, often at speed, and North America will keep you honest about that: a solo clinic in Texas, a hospital network in Ontario, and a group practice in California are all operating under different rules, different documentation norms, and different expectations of what "done" looks like.

Your job is to find the shape that works across all of it without the product fragmenting into a hundred one-offs, or flattening into something that fits nobody well. You'll own the connective tissue of the product — shared patterns, consistent feel, the details that make software feel like one product, even when it's being pulled in a dozen directions by a dozen customers at once. You'll partner directly with engineers, push code when it makes sense, and care about the 3px padding issue as much as the information architecture.

- Design and ship features in direct response to live customer requests, often turning a raw ask into a considered solution within days, not sprints
- Work across many customers and many countries at once, and know when a local nuance deserves its own path versus when it's a sign the core pattern needs to flex
- Own design quality across the product — catch what's inconsistent and fix it before it ships

Someone downloads Co–Star every 5 seconds.

In the five years since we launched, 25% of young people 18-25 in the US have downloaded the app. Big Sean has rapped about us, Ariana Grande & Kevin Durant post screenshots to their IGs, and we've been App of the Day twice. Astrology has been popular for 4,000 years.

Astrology is a tool for speaking about yourself, about who you are, what you're experiencing, and how you relate to other people – in other words, a language for the things that really matter. We're merging the resonance of the humanities with the precision of technology.

title: UX Designer, AI App
description:
About A1
There are over 5 billion users using basic applications today such email, notes, tasks that are not AI-native. Our mission is to build a proactive smart assistant for everyday users to bring intelligence to conversations, errands, organising and workflows, with minimal prompting.
Our product focuses on achieving high reliability for long-running workflows, persistent context, and real-world task completion. The system must handle multi-step reasoning, interact with external tools, and remain reliable despite non-deterministic model behavior. Our objective is to help users complete tasks daily enjoyable with over ~90%* reduced time.


Role
You will own the UX of A1's core app experience. This means designing the end-to-end flows users go through every day - how they start tasks, how they follow along as the AI works, how they stay in control, and how they recover when something goes wrong.
This is a UX role for a HCI product. You need to understand both user needs and AI system behavior well enough to design product flows that feel clear, reliable, and controllable.


What You'll Be Doing

- Own UX for A1's core app surfaces across iOS, Android, and web.
- Design complete user flows for AI-assisted tasks - from intent capture through to task completion, including handoff, progress tracking, and error recovery.
- Design how the app surfaces what the AI is doing, what decisions it has made, and what the user needs to confirm or adjust.
- Map and design the full range of AI states a user encounters - loading, thinking, acting, waiting, completing, stalling, failing, and recovering.
- Work with product, engineering, and ML teams to define user requirements and translate them into concrete design solutions.
- Conduct usability research to understand where users lose trust, feel uncertain, or disengage.
- Produce wireframes, user flows, and high-fidelity designs that engineering can build from directly.
- Contribute to the design system and shared UX patterns for AI app surfaces.
- Design for both simple everyday interactions and complex multi-step AI workflows within the same product.


What You Will Need

- Experience as a UX designer on consumer mobile or web apps, with a strong portfolio.
- Solid skills in user flow design, wireframing, and high-fidelity prototyping in Figma.
- Ability to design for systems that are asynchronous, non-deterministic, and context-dependent.
- Clear thinking about user trust, control, feedback, and transparency in AI-driven product experiences.
- Experience conducting user research and turning findings into design decisions.
- Comfortable working in fast-moving teams with evolving product scope.
- Ability to balance simple consumer UX with complex AI system behavior.
- Good judgment on usability, edge cases, failure handling, and recovery flows.


How We Work
The best products today in the world were built by small, world class teams. We are a high talent density and hands-on team. We make decisions collective

title: Design Lead
description:
About The Job

Midjourney is an independent research lab exploring new mediums of thought and expanding the imaginative powers of the human species. We are a small, self-funded team focused on design, human infrastructure, and AI.

We don't think the future should look like yesterday's software. Our design team works across research, engineering, and product to make new capabilities feel intuitive, fun to use, and deeply human.

We're looking for a Design Lead to help lead that effort.

You'll partner closely with our Chief Design Officer to shape the future of Midjourney's products while building and leading the product design team.

This isn't a traditional management role. You’ll spend meaningful time designing, prototyping, reviewing work, and solving difficult product problems alongside your team. Most days you will be helping exceptional designers do the best work of their careers by building with them. If your favorite part of leadership is modeling what good looks like by collaborating and getting your hands dirty with your team, you’ll probably enjoy it here.

What you'll do



- Work closely with the Chief Design Officer to shape the direction of Midjourney's products. 
- Recruit, mentor, and lead the product design team. 
- Stay close to the work by designing key product experiences and helping teams solve their hardest design problems. 
- Partner closely with engineering and research to turn new tech into intuitive product experiences. 
- Establish design reviews and operating rhythms that help the team do its best work. 
- Ensure a coherent experience across Midjourney's growing portfolio of products. 

You might be a fit if



- You've spent the last decade designing software people love to use. 
- You've led design teams, but you still want to be in Figma every day. 
- You're as comfortable thinking through product strategy as you are refining a single interaction. 
- You work well with engineers and like building things that don't have established playbooks. 
- You care about craft and iterate until something feels right. 
- You're comfortable using tools like Claude Code and Cursor as part of your workflow. 
- You believe the best work comes from showing work early and often, and collaboratively iterating on unfinished work
- You're excited by the idea that AI requires entirely new interaction paradigms, not just new features. 
- Work > ego
- Prototypes > presentations

Logistics



- Full-time. San Francisco Hybrid. 
- Compensation: $285,000–$350,000 + benefits

To apply

A portfolio is required.

We care much more about what you've made than where you've worked. If this role excites you, we'd love to hear from you—even if you don't check every box.

Amazon Robotics is seeking a Senior Product Designer to lead the design of experiences that span the digital and physical worlds, from the screen-based tools technicians use to diagnose robotic systems, to the physical touchpoints, labels, and spatial workflows they navigate on the fulfillment center floor.

You'll define what "Exceptional UX" means in an environment where the user's hands are often occupied, and every second of downtime costs throughput. This means designing not just pixels, but the full interaction arc: how a technician receives an alert, locates the problem, accesses the right information, performs the repair, and confirms resolution.

-  Design across the digital-physical spectrum including screen-based diagnostic tools, hardware interface panels, and spatial wayfinding.

-  Create scalable mechanisms and reusable design patterns that multiply team impact across multiple robotics programs.
-  Map end-to-end service journeys that account for body posture, environment, tool-in-hand constraints, and transitions between digital interfaces and physical tasks
-  Lead UX research efforts with our product partners in the field through contextual inquiry on the warehouse floor, shadowing technicians during repairs, and observing how physical environment shapes interaction with digital tools
-  Partner cross-functionally with hardware engineering, software engineering, product management, industrial design, and operations to ensure physical and digital touchpoints are coherent
-  Mentor junior designers and elevate UX maturity across the organization
-  Advocate for the end user by bringing field-grounded insights into roadmap and prioritization discussions
-  Synthesize quantitative operational data with qualitative field insights to inform design priorities and trade-offs
-  Produce written and visual artifacts that influence product roadmaps and senior leadership decisions

A day in the life

As a Senior Product Designer on the Amazon Robotics team, you'll shape how people interact with advanced robotic systems across Amazon's fulfillment network. Your focus is designing the interfaces and workflows technicians use to diagnose and maintain robots, creating a seamless connection between what's on screen and what's happening on the floor.

You'll conduct field research, create prototypes, design compelling experiences, and collaborate closely with software engineers, product managers, industrial designers, and human factors engineers. This is a role for someone who thinks in systems and first principles, not just screens.

title: Sr. Product Designer, Amazon Robotics

Description

Amazon Robotics is seeking a Senior Product Designer to lead the design of experiences that span the digital and physical worlds, from the screen-based tools technicians use to diagnose robotic systems, to the physical touchpoints, labels, and spatial workflows they navigate on the fulfillment center floor.

You'll define what "Exceptional UX" means in an environment where the user's hands are often occupied, and every second of downtime costs throughput. This means designing not just pixels, but the full interaction arc: how a technician receives an alert, locates the problem, accesses the right information, performs the repair, and confirms resolution.

Key job responsibilities



-  Design across the digital-physical spectrum including screen-based diagnostic tools, hardware interface panels, and spatial wayfinding.
-  Define interaction models for complex, data-rich interfaces optimized for gloved hands.
-  Design for the senses by considering visual, auditory, and haptic feedback in environments where a screen may not be the primary channel
-  Create scalable mechanisms and reusable design patterns that multiply team impact across multiple robotics programs.
-  Map end-to-end service journeys that account for body posture, environment, tool-in-hand constraints, and transitions between digital interfaces and physical tasks
-  Lead UX research efforts with our product partners in the field through contextual inquiry on the warehouse floor, shadowing technicians during repairs, and observing how physical environment shapes interaction with digital tools
-  Partner cross-functionally with hardware engineering, software engineering, product management, industrial design, and operations to ensure physical and digital touchpoints are coherent
-  Mentor junior designers and elevate UX maturity across the organization
-  Advocate for the end user by bringing field-grounded insights into roadmap and prioritization discussions
-  Synthesize quantitative operational data with qualitative field insights to inform design priorities and trade-offs
-  Produce written and visual artifacts that influence product roadmaps and senior leadership decisions

A day in the life

As a Senior Product Designer on the Amazon Robotics team, you'll shape how people interact with advanced robotic systems across Amazon's fulfillment network. Your focus is designing the interfaces and workflows technicians use to diagnose and maintain robots, creating a seamless connection between what's on screen and what's happening on the floor.

You'll conduct field research, create prototypes, design compelling experiences, and collaborate closely with software engineers, product managers, industrial designers, and human factors engineers. This is a role for someone who thinks in systems and first principles, not just screens.
